meta.subtitle: Fiscal 2026: AI infrastructure orders lift growth, but memory costs and a full multiple keep the call at HOLD

analystCommentary:
Cisco closed fiscal 2026 with revenue of $63.3B, up 12% on the company's figures, and GAAP diluted EPS of $3.33, up 31%. The growth was product-led, and the recurring lines and gross margin did not keep pace, as covered under Financials.

The demand evidence is strong. The August 12, 2026 earnings release reports Q4 product orders up 35% year over year (up 25% excluding hyperscalers), AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers of $9.3 billion for fiscal 2026, and an expected $7.5 billion of AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers in fiscal 2027. Management guides fiscal 2027 revenue to $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion.

The price already reflects much of this. At $112.82 the stock trades at 21.9x consensus FY27E EPS of $5.15, which sits above the top of the company's non-GAAP guidance, and at 33.9x trailing GAAP earnings. Our probability-weighted value sits modestly above the price but short of the BUY threshold, and the bear case, a stall in earnings with a lower multiple, is a plausible outcome rather than a tail. We rate CSCO HOLD with a 12-month target range of $105 to $140.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Cisco Systems designs and sells networking, security, collaboration and observability technology, plus the services that support it, to businesses, public institutions, governments and service providers. It sells directly and through systems integrators, service providers, resellers and distributors, and was incorporated in 1984.

The company reports as a single reportable segment, with fiscal 2026 revenue of $63.3B. The 10-K says it is incorporating AI into its portfolios and integrating its products more tightly into a platform.

thesis.body: Hyperscaler AI and campus networking demand has lifted Cisco's growth, but the growth is hardware-led, gross margin and free cash flow moved the wrong way, and the forward multiple already discounts the guide. The weighted outcome sits a little above the price, so we rate HOLD; the full argument is in the analyst commentary and Valuation.

catalysts: Delivery of the $7.5 billion of hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue the company expects in fiscal 2027; see Growth.
Q1 fiscal 2027 results against guidance of $18.0 billion to $18.2 billion of revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $1.32 to $1.34.
Non-GAAP gross margin holding inside the guided 65% - 66% range for Q1 fiscal 2027 despite memory costs; see Risks.
Order growth outside hyperscalers, which the release puts at 25% in Q4 fiscal 2026; see Growth.
risks: Customer concentration in hyperscaler AI demand, about 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue; see Risks.
Memory constraints and costs squeezing product gross margin; see Risks.
Inventory and purchase-commitment exposure if demand slows; see Risks.
A forward multiple that already discounts the guided growth; see Valuation.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Fiscal 2026 revenue rose to $63.3B, up 12% on the company's figures (the vendor table shows +11.8%), after +5.3% in FY25 and -5.6% in FY24. For Q4 fiscal 2026 the company reports revenue up 18% year over year to $17.3 billion; the vendor snapshot shows +16%, and we use the company's figure.

The mix shifted toward hardware. Product revenue rose 16% while services revenue was flat; total software revenue was $23.2 billion, up 4%, and subscription revenue rose 1%.

Full-year gross margin slipped to 64.5% from 64.9%. The company explains the {- 0.5 percentage point -} decline in product gross margin by product mix and higher memory costs. In Q4 the two bases moved in opposite directions: GAAP gross margin rose to 64.1% from 63.2%, which the company attributes mainly to the absence of the prior-year supplier charge and to favorable pricing, while non-GAAP gross margin fell to 66.3% from 68.4%. Because the GAAP gain rests largely on a charge not recurring, we treat the non-GAAP decline as the cleaner read on mix and memory costs.

Research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses fell by {+ 3.4 percentage points +} of revenue, and operating margin rose to 24.3% from 20.8%. The company attributes the 31% rise in diluted EPS to revenue growth and operating margin improvement. Below the operating line, other income (loss), net moved from a loss of $68 million in fiscal 2025 to a gain of $1,245 million in fiscal 2026, $822 million of it in Q4. The excerpt does not explain this non-operating gain. It flatters fiscal 2026 GAAP EPS, its growth rate and the 33.9x trailing P/E, and we do not extrapolate it.

GAAP and non-GAAP earnings diverge widely: fiscal 2026 non-GAAP EPS was $4.33, and fiscal 2027 guidance is GAAP $4.00 to $4.06 against non-GAAP $5.05 to $5.11. Restructuring and other charges were $693 million for the year. The income statement is healthier than a year ago, but the improvement rests on hardware volume and expense leverage rather than gross margin.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt was $29.5B at fiscal year-end, up from $28.1B. Short-term debt rose to $10,161 million from $5,232 million, so a larger share of borrowings now falls due within a year. The vendor's net debt of $22.3B is total debt minus cash and cash equivalents only; we use that basis. The company reports cash and cash equivalents and investments of $15.9 billion, which would leave a smaller net figure if investments were counted, while the vendor's cash and short-term investments line shows $14.3B; the two differ in what they include.

Inventories rose to $5,694 million from $3,164 million, and the 10-K excerpt does not explain the rise; the relevant risk-factor language is under Risks. The provision for inventory and purchase commitments fell to $387 million from $493 million, so the build has not yet raised write-down charges. Whether the new inventory is fully saleable remains open.

The current ratio is 0.93, below 1.00 in FY25, and interest coverage on trailing figures is 10.5x. Equity rose to $50.3B. The balance sheet is serviceable, but the inventory build and heavier short-term maturities make it less flexible than a year ago.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow was $14.2 billion in fiscal 2026, flat on fiscal 2025, even as net income rose 30%. Capital expenditure increased to $1.4B from $0.9B, so free cash flow fell to $12.8B from $13.3B and FCF margin fell to 20.2% from 23.5%. Earnings growth has therefore not yet reached cash; the inventory build discussed above is one likely use of working capital, although the excerpt does not break it down, and part of the net income rise came from the non-operating gain, which need not produce matching operating cash.

Share repurchases of $6.1B and dividends of $6.6B together absorbed nearly all of fiscal 2026 free cash flow. That pace leaves little internal funding for acquisitions or debt reduction without slowing buybacks. The trailing FCF yield of 2.9% is thin for a company of this maturity and is the main reason we do not treat the cash return as a valuation floor.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing GAAP earnings CSCO trades at 33.9x, with EV/EBITDA of 24.7x and P/S of 7.0x. The vendor's forward P/E of 21.9x labelled NTM matches the price over consensus FY27E EPS of $5.15, so it is effectively a current-fiscal-year multiple; on FY28E EPS of $5.62 the forward P/E is ~20.1x. Both forward figures rest on consensus estimates that sit above the top of the company's non-GAAP FY27 guidance, so they are non-GAAP multiples, not GAAP ones.

Peer multiples are not available here, and we do not use them. The trailing GAAP multiple is inflated relative to the forward one because fiscal 2026 GAAP EPS carries amortization and restructuring that the non-GAAP figures exclude, partly offset by the non-operating gain covered under Financials. The forward multiple is reasonable for revenue growth the company guides into the mid-teens, but it is not cheap for a business whose recurring lines are growing slowly and whose free cash flow fell.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Hyperscaler AI orders keep compounding, fiscal 2027 lands at or above the top of guidance, and non-GAAP gross margin holds near Q4 levels. The market pays a multiple in the mid-to-high twenties on FY28E EPS of $5.62, still below the Street high target of $170.00.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Cisco meets fiscal 2027 guidance and the FY28E consensus EPS used in Bull holds. Today's 21.9x forward multiple rolls onto that FY28E figure over 12 months, a value below the consensus target of $136.16.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: A de-rating with stalled earnings: hyperscaler orders pause and memory costs keep pressing gross margin, so EPS lands at the low end of FY27 non-GAAP guidance, $5.05, and does not grow into fiscal 2028. With no FY28 growth to roll onto, the market prices that figure at a high-teens multiple.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We value CSCO over a 12-month horizon on non-GAAP EPS, because that is the basis of consensus and of the forward multiples; GAAP EPS is lower, as covered under Financials. Base at $123 is the simplest checkable case: today's forward multiple on FY27E rolls forward onto FY28E consensus EPS. Bull at $150 needs both upside to guidance and a higher multiple on the same FY28E figure. Bear at $90 uses a different EPS year on purpose: it assumes earnings stall at the bottom of the FY27 guidance range with no growth into fiscal 2028, so that figure is the forward base a year from now, and it applies a high-teens multiple. Most of the Bear downside therefore comes from the multiple, not from earnings. The shares traded as low as $66.81 within the past year, and the Street low target of $110.00 is too close to the price to serve as a real downside.

We weight Bull and Bear equally at 25% each, with 50% on Base. The case for more Bull weight is real: Q4 orders, the gap between fiscal 2026 hyperscaler orders and revenue, and a fiscal 2027 guide calling for faster growth. The case against is equally concrete: a fast-growing part of the growth comes from hyperscaler hardware, the Q4 non-GAAP gross margin decline and the fall in free cash flow covered under Financials, and a stock that has already risen from its 52-week low toward the $130.37 high.

The call is reasonably close. Shifting five points of weight from Bear to Bull would lift the expected return to around the BUY threshold with reward/risk near its floor. We do not think that shift is justified until gross margin shows it can hold through the memory cycle, so the derived label is HOLD.

The target range of $105 to $140 brackets Base and spans moderate downside to a value near the Street consensus.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Cisco reports a single reportable segment, so all of fiscal 2026 revenue of $63.3B sits here. Product revenue was led by Networking at 22% growth, which the company ties particularly to AI Infrastructure and Campus Networking. Security product revenue grew 2% for the year but 14% in Q4 fiscal 2026, Collaboration 4% and Observability 4%. The shift toward hardware and the slower recurring lines are covered under Financials.

moatFactors.name: Installed base and services attach
moatFactors.body: Remaining performance obligations were $46.7 billion at fiscal year-end, up 7%, and deferred revenue was $29.8 billion, up 3%. Contracted revenue of that size gives visibility and reflects a large installed base that buys support and renewals. The counter-point is the slow recurring lines covered under Financials, so the base is stable rather than expanding.

moatFactors.name: Networking scale and breadth
moatFactors.body: Cisco sells across campus, data center, wireless, service-provider and hyperscaler networks, and the release reports Networking product orders up 40% in Q4 fiscal 2026, an eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Breadth lets it bundle security and observability into the platform. The risk factors note that price and product competition can change rapidly with technological innovation, so scale does not guarantee share in new AI architectures.

moatFactors.name: Pricing power
moatFactors.body: The company credits pricing actions with partly offsetting gross margin pressure, which shows some ability to pass on costs. Yet product gross margin still fell on mix and memory costs, and the Q4 non-GAAP read covered under Financials points the same way. Pricing protects gross margin at the edges rather than insulating it.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The installed base, the remaining performance obligations and the breadth of the networking portfolio are durable advantages, and they let Cisco participate in hyperscaler AI build-outs without being a newcomer. Growth was broad in fiscal 2026: campus networking grew alongside AI infrastructure, and orders outside hyperscalers also rose strongly, as covered under Growth. Hyperscalers are still a small share of revenue, but a meaningful and fast-growing part of the growth is hardware sold to them, which the company itself links to customer concentration and where the risk factors describe rapid price and technology competition. Together with slow growth in the recurring lines, that keeps the moat narrower than the revenue scale suggests. A widening would show up as subscription and services growth catching up with product growth; a narrowing as gross margin erosion that pricing cannot offset.

points: Hyperscaler AI infrastructure is a major driver. The August 12, 2026 release reports $9.3 billion of such orders in fiscal 2026, including $4 billion in Q4, approximately $4 billion of related revenue in fiscal 2026 and $7.5 billion expected in fiscal 2027. The 10-K puts hyperscalers at approximately 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue, up from less than 2% in fiscal 2025, and the company expects this demand to remain a significant driver in fiscal 2027.

Demand is broadening beyond hyperscalers. Q4 fiscal 2026 product orders rose 35% year over year and 25% excluding hyperscalers, with double-digit growth across every geography and customer market per the release. Orders lead revenue, so this supports the near-term guide; it does not show how durable the cycle is.

Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion, consistent with consensus FY27E revenue of ~$73.2B (+16%). Consensus then expects FY28E revenue of $78.1B, so growth continues but slows sharply in fiscal 2028. In our view part of fiscal 2027 may be pulled forward by the hyperscaler orders already booked, which would make the fiscal 2028 slowdown a fair base rather than a conservative one.

Software and security are the slower legs, as the fiscal 2026 product mix shows. In Q4 the company closed two acquisitions, Galileo Technologies (observability) and Astrix Securities (Non-Human Identity security); the release does not disclose their size, so their contribution to growth cannot yet be judged.

The main constraint on growth is supply and cost. The 10-K cites a highly competitive and complex environment, especially memory constraints and costs and trade policy, so component availability could cap how much of the order book converts on schedule.

management.leadership: Chuck Robbins is Chair and CEO, and Mark Patterson is CFO, per the August 12, 2026 earnings release. The fiscal 2025 proxy, filed October 28, 2025, lists R. Scott Herren as former Executive Vice President and CFO, and names Jeetendra (Jeetu) Patel as President and Chief Product Officer. Management's stated focus for fiscal 2027 is durable growth, consistent profitability and continued capital returns while investing in growth opportunities. Execution in fiscal 2026 was good: the release says Q4 revenue, non-GAAP operating income and EPS all exceeded the high end of guidance. The test now is margin management through the memory cycle rather than demand generation.
management.capitalAllocation: Cisco returns most of its free cash flow. In Q4 fiscal 2026 it returned $3.2 billion through buybacks and dividends, repurchasing approximately 13 million shares at an average price of $111.53, close to today's price. The remaining repurchase authorization is $8.1 billion with no termination date, and the board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share, payable October 21, 2026; future dividends remain subject to board approval. Buybacks at prices near the current level look reasonable against our Base value but not compelling. Given the cash flow and balance-sheet trends discussed under Financials, we would prefer the company not lean on borrowing to sustain the return pace.
management.governance: Per the fiscal 2025 proxy filed October 28, 2025, all directors other than Mr. Robbins are independent, all members of the Audit, Compensation and Nomination and Governance Committees are independent, and Mr. Capellas serves as Lead Independent Director while Mr. Robbins combines the Chair and CEO roles. The combined role concentrates authority, which the board offsets with a lead independent director who chairs executive sessions. That October 2025 proxy reports approximately 77% say-on-pay support at the previous year's meeting, up from approximately 75%; no later vote result is available here. That is passing but soft support, and the proxy says the company engaged holders of approximately 61% of shares partly in response. We view governance as adequate, with pay alignment the item to monitor.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt available here carries no beneficial-ownership table, so we cannot assess insider stakes. No holder is identified as having a controlling position.

idiosyncratic: Hyperscaler concentration: the company itself flags the customer concentration and supply considerations tied to AI infrastructure demand, which it expects to remain a significant driver in fiscal 2027. The risk factors note that demand from service providers and cloud customers fluctuates and that large orders can swing a quarter. A pause by a few buyers would hit both revenue and the order narrative. Monitor quarterly hyperscaler order figures against the fiscal 2027 revenue expectation.

Memory costs and gross margin: product gross margin fell on mix and higher memory costs, and the company describes memory constraints as part of a complex environment. Hardware-heavy AI revenue may carry lower gross margin than the rest of the mix. Monitor non-GAAP gross margin against the 65% - 66% Q1 fiscal 2027 range.

Inventory and commitments: the risk factors say that when managing component supply challenges Cisco has in the past, and may in the future, increase procurement, which increases inventory and purchase commitments. Separately, the risk factor on economic conditions lists a risk of excess and obsolete inventories in a slowdown. Together these make the fiscal 2026 inventory build discussed under Financials a liability if demand cools. Monitor inventory levels and the provision for inventory and purchase commitments.

Earnings quality and restructuring: GAAP EPS runs well below non-GAAP EPS, and the risk factors say changes in the business model could result in significant restructuring charges; Q4 fiscal 2026 restructuring and other charges rose to $511 million from $35 million. Repeated charges would keep the GAAP multiple elevated. Monitor restructuring charges and the GAAP to non-GAAP gap.

Refinancing and liquidity: with more debt falling due within a year and a current ratio below 1.0, as discussed under Financials, Cisco must refinance or repay that short-term debt. Interest coverage is comfortable today, but higher rates would raise interest cost. Monitor the mix of short-term debt and the use of cash for buybacks.
risks.systemic: The risk factors cite tariffs and other trade barriers, inflation, central bank policy uncertainty, and geopolitical instability including the Russia and Ukraine war, Middle East conflicts and China-Taiwan relations. These may reduce IT spending by service provider, cloud and enterprise customers, increase price competition, and create excess inventory or supply constraints. Cisco's exposure runs through enterprise and service-provider capital budgets and through its supply chain for components such as memory. An AI capital-spending slowdown across the industry would hit the hyperscaler business first, while a broad recession would hit enterprise and campus demand.

body: HOLD, 12-month target range $105 to $140, for the reasons set out in the analyst commentary and Valuation: strong orders and expense discipline, offset by hardware-led growth, weaker gross margin and free cash flow, and a price that already reflects the guide.

We would move to BUY if non-GAAP gross margin finishes fiscal 2027 at or above the top of the 65% - 66% Q1 guided range while revenue tracks the upper half of the $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion guide, or if the price fell toward our Bear value without a change in the outlook. We would move to SELL if the company cut its fiscal 2027 hyperscaler AI revenue expectation below $7.5 billion or lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance.
